benefit.name: Work-Able Accessible Employment Program (BC Public Service)
benefit.amount: Paid BC Public Service internship of up to 24 months
benefit.summary: A paid internship program in the BC Public Service for recent post-secondary graduates who self-identify as having a disability. This can be any physical, sensory, neurological, visible or invisible disability.

items: You are a recent post-secondary graduate with a two-year diploma, associate degree, bachelor's degree, master's degree or doctorate from a recognized post-secondary institution.
Your graduation date is within 3 years of the program start date.
You self-identify as having a disability.
eligibility.note: You do not have to disclose your specific diagnosis.

benefit.requiresNote: You must be a recent post-secondary graduate with a two-year diploma, associate degree, bachelor's degree, master's degree or doctorate from a recognized post-secondary institution, with a graduation date within 3 years of the program start date, and self-identify as having a disability. You do not have to disclose your specific diagnosis.
benefit.note: Intake runs every year. Applications for the 2026/27 cohort are closed. The page says to check back in Spring 2027 for information on the 2027/28 intake. Graduates keep access to internal BC Public Service job postings for 24 months after they finish the program.

detail.about: Work-Able coordinates paid internship opportunities across the BC Public Service for recent graduates with disabilities, for up to 24 months. Participants get government work experience, a peer cohort of other graduates with disabilities, exposure to different career paths, and post-program access to internal job postings.
steps: Check the Work-Able page in Spring 2027 for information on the 2027/28 intake, or contact the Work-Able team to be notified when the next application period opens.
Confirm you graduated within 3 years of the program start date.
Apply online during the intake window; you self-identify as having a disability without disclosing a diagnosis.
If selected, you are placed in a paid position with a ministry.
documents: Proof of post-secondary graduation (within 3 years of program start)
tips: Contact the Work-Able team to be notified when the next application period opens.
Workplace accommodations are part of the program's design, so you do not need to negotiate them alone.
detail.time: Annual intake; internships run up to 24 months

values.note: paid BC Public Service internship (up to 24 months)

meta.effort: Online application during an open intake
